children: weighed by surging global yields and oil prices Our Bureau Mumbai: Indian equity benchmarks lost for the seventh straight week, burdened by surging global yields and oil prices, although the gauges eked out modest gains Friday. The Nifty 50 gained 77.40 points, or 0.34%, to close at 23,140.50, while the Sensex rose 315.20 points, or 0.43%, to end at 73,895.74. For the week, the Nifty declined 0.9% and the Sensex fell 0.5%. On BSE, 2,210 stocks advanced and 2,146 declined. Auto and consumer durables stocks gained nearly 0.9% each, while realty rose 0.76% and private banks advanced 0.45%. IT, media, oil and gas and pharma stocks ended lower. In the broader market, the Nifty midcap index slipped 0.15%, while the smallcap index gained 0.02%. India VIX, the market's volatility gauge, declined 4%. "Seven straight weekly losses, and the India VIX still ended the week below 12 and the Nifty is now about 12% below its January record, but this has been a grind, not a rout," said Gaurav Garg, head of research, Lemonn. "It is an orderly de-rating driven by crude above $100, a Federal Reserve that is hiking rather than cutting, and US bond yields at multi-decade highs," he said.

Brent crude hovered around $105.5 a barrel as investors weighed the possibility of a truce between the US and Iran against concerns over increasing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi rebels. A stronger dollar, energy-supply risks, geopolitical uncertainty and sustained foreign institutional selling continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

The rupee closed at 95.8125 against the US dollar, marginally stronger than its previous close of 95.9550. Garg said foreign investors had already pulled more money from Indian equities this year than in all of 2025 despite the June-quarter earnings having beaten estimates. He said a credible agreement between the US and Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz could bring down crude prices and trigger short-covering in heavily sold large-cap stocks, particularly banks.

However, insurance and insurance-distribution stocks continue to face a separate regulatory overhang following the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's (IRDAI) proposed changes on commissions. The proposal has weighed on PB Fintech and other companies in the insurance-distribution segment.

Banks and IT stocks remained among the key weekly drags, falling 1.4% and 2.4%, respectively. On the technical front, the Sensex continued to form bearish candles on the weekly chart, with lower lows for the fourth consecutive week, indicating continued pressure on the broader trend, according to Chandan Taparia, Head of Technical & Derivatives Research at Motilal Financial Services.

title: India's Equity Indices on a Losing Streak for Seventh Straight Week
